text: The following question stood in the name of  Mr Christopher de Souza 	–  9 To ask the Minister for Home Affairs whether there is an upward trend of drug syndicates exploiting minors in the drug trade and how can our enforcement actions and statutory framework deter the syndicates from doing so.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what is the Ministry’s position on the research paper entitled “Costs of Drug Crime: Literature Review and Methodology” which calculated the detriment drugs cause to Singapore society; (b) whether the findings provide further impetus for Singapore to advance its war on drugs; and (c) what will be done to ensure that a tough and deterrent stance is taken against drug traffickers who push drugs into and within Singapore.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Can someone ask the Question on his behalf?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Drugs destroy lives and impose immense costs on individuals and society.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Besides tangible costs, such as physical injuries, lost productivity and cost of incarceration, there are also very significant intangible costs, in terms of lost lives, pain and suffering, and untold misery to families.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The research paper attempted to quantify the costs to Singapore of drug crime, both tangible and intangible costs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This is almost certainly an underestimation, as there are other costs which were not included in the study, such as the number of workdays lost for victims of drug crimes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The report did not include this data because it has not been quantified.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The high costs drugs impose on society is one reason why we must maintain our firm stance against drugs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have put in place tough laws and maintain intensive enforcement.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We have strengthened our legislative framework and enhanced our enforcement powers to better protect young persons from being exploited and becoming victims of drugs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In addition, adult traffickers who are found to be trafficking to young persons would face tougher penalties.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It is also now an offence for an adult to permit or not take reasonable steps to prevent a young person from consuming illicit drugs in the adult’s possession.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will continue to tighten our legislation as needed.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The question is, in light of the statistic that the highest number of new drug abusers are below 35 and in light of the growing calls, at least around the world – not in Singapore but around the world – to legalise recreational drug use, and in addition to that, this cost of drug crime study, how can we use these statistics and facts to bolster our position against drug trafficking into Singapore?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And in addition to that, to assist drug consumers to rehabilitate and not be recalcitrant?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, deterring both the supply and the demand, in light of these facts and statistics.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Indeed, the push for drug legalisation around the world is a cause for concern.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As the Member may already know, in October 2018, Canada became the second country in the world, after Uruguay, to legalise the use of cannabis for recreational purposes.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In January 2019, the World Health Organization (WHO) Expert Committee on Drug Dependence also made six recommendations on the international scheduling of cannabis and cannabis-related substances.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We hope to add to the literature so that more are aware about what are the drug-involved crimes as well as drug-attributable crimes, and what the cost to society are.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In time, the researchers are preparing for this paper for publication in international journals.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: At the same time, we are also stepping up our education outreach.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We understand that preventive drug education is definitely the first line of defence when it comes to drug control.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Member had mentioned some trends whereby young people are increasingly prone towards certain messages they may receive over social media about drugs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, social media is a key platform for us to reach out to youths.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: CNB has been developing content messages of strong deterrence, as well as evidence-based narratives on Singapore's drug policies through its social media accounts.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: At the end of the day, what we are going to do is going to be guided by research.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: At the same time, we are also pushing out our education outreach efforts to make sure that for high-risk youths and persons of certain segments, we reach out to them actively with the anti-drug message.
